issues.title: Incorrect evaluation of the shifted exponential tail moment
issues.failure_explanation: After setting s=t−T and a=2m0απ, the relevant factor is ∫_0^∞(s+a)^l e^(−s/κ) ds. It equals κ for l=0 and κ(a+κ) for l=1, hence κ(a+κ)^l for l∈{0,1}. The old proof instead uses κ(2κm0απ)^l and then κ^(l+1)T^l under only T≥a. For l=1 the final comparison requires T≥a/κ+1, which was not assumed in the lemma.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma infty's explicit tail estimate has an invalid calculation, leaving a local gap in the quadrature-error chain. The corrected term is still exponentially smaller than the dominant error.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In Lemma infty, set a=2m0απ and replace the faulty tail evaluation by ∫₀^∞(s+a)^l e^(−s/κ) ds=κ(a+κ)^l for l∈{0,1}. Carry this corrected constant into eq:intestall; since it multiplies e^(−2nT), it remains bounded by O(T^l e^(−2nT)) for large T, so the quadrature theorem and all listed approximation rates remain unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The proof contains a genuine integration error, so this is not merely transcriptional. Its repair is an elementary local calculation affecting only an exponentially subordinate constant, with no new lemma, proof architecture, rate loss, or weakening anywhere in the affected chain.

issues.title: Extraneous 2−β factor in the residue geometric ratio
issues.failure_explanation: In eq:res1 the j-dependent exponent contains 4j−2−θ. Increasing j by one changes this quantity by exactly 4, so the geometric ratio is exp(−8nπ²αA/h), independently of β. Old asy0000 instead uses exp(−8nπ²α(2−β)A/h). For β<1 this gives a denominator that is too large and therefore an invalid upper bound.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the lower-pole residue estimate is invalid on an admissible part of the β range, leaving the residue and quadrature bounds unsupported until the ratio is corrected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Let R=T+α log(x/C) and sum the j-terms using the actual ratio exp(−8nπ²αR/h), replacing the denominator in asy0000 by 1−exp(−8nπ²αR/h). The existing lower bound on R and the existing x-regime estimates then recover the same two residual bounds, which propagate unchanged through the quadrature and approximation theorems.
issues.why_classification: The wrong geometric ratio is an invalid proof inference rather than a harmless statement typo. Recomputing the ratio and its denominator is nevertheless short, routine, and local, and it changes only constants rather than the residue exponent, convergence rates, domains, or guarantees of the affected chain.

issues.title: Wrong Fourier sign at lower-half-plane poles
issues.failure_explanation: For a lower-half-plane pole u=a−ib with a,b>0, |exp(+icu²)|=exp(2cab) grows, whereas |exp(−icu²)|=exp(−2cab) decays. The old asy00odd statement uses the positive sign, while eq:res1 and the lower-contour residue term in eq:fourier_cpath calculate and use the negative sign.
issues.overall_effect: The first residue estimate is wrong as stated, although the proof already establishes the correctly signed estimate used by the later contour calculation.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In asy00odd, replace the Fourier factor at each lower-half-plane pole by exp(−i2nπu²/h). No proof or downstream statement otherwise needs alteration.
issues.why_classification: The negative sign is uniquely forced by eq:res1 and the lower-contour residue term in eq:fourier_cpath, both of which already use it. The proof establishes the correctly signed estimate, so the positive sign in the lemma statement is a transcriptional statement–proof mismatch.

issues.title: Missing h normalization in the Case 2 Fourier coefficient
issues.failure_explanation: The first line of old eq:fourier_cnew correctly expresses c_n as 1/h times two integrals. The following contour representation omits that 1/h without any compensating multiplication, so the equality is false. The Case 1 identities correctly use the normalization hc_n, and the latest Case 2 calculation does the same.
issues.overall_effect: The exact Case 2 Fourier-coefficient identity is off by the fixed factor h. Because h=σ²α² is fixed as T grows, this does not change the claimed convergence orders.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Write the Case 2 contour identity as an identity for hc_n, or equivalently retain a factor 1/h on every contour and residue term on its right-hand side. Use that consistently in the subsequent Poisson sum.
issues.why_classification: The preceding line defining c_n, the change of variables, and the analogous Case 1 identity uniquely force this normalization. The omitted factor is transcriptional; restoring it requires no change to the contour argument and, with h fixed as T grows, does not alter any convergence order.

issues.title: Invalid denominator bound on the complex contour
issues.failure_explanation: In Case 1 let β=0, 0<α<1, m=l=0, z=x>0, and r=C exp((√h−T)/α). The Case 1 condition gives x>er. At the admissible contour value t=πα, the denominator is x−r, so the relevant ratio is x/(x−r)>1. The old eq:l1 bounds this ratio by 1/X(0)=1, which is false. The real-axis estimate eq:est does not apply after the exponential acquires a complex phase.
issues.overall_effect: The uniform contour estimate used in the proof of the quadrature theorem is invalid as printed, so its subsequent Fourier-coefficient bound lacks support.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace eq:l1 by a contour-specific denominator estimate using the Case 1 pole separation. The identities involving u(1,0) and u(1,k) give bounds of the form |z/(Ce^((√h−it−T)/α)+z)|≤(1−e^(−1))^(−1) and corresponding bounds for every interpolation denominator, yielding the same O(T^l e^(−T)) estimate with an additional fixed factor such as (1−e^(−1))^(−m−1). Substitute this bound in the vertical-contour estimate and retain all downstream rates.
issues.why_classification: The old proof genuinely misapplies a real-axis denominator bound on a complex contour. However, the required pole-separation inequalities are already supplied by the Case 1 hypotheses, and inserting the resulting fixed constant is a short local repair that preserves the method, uniformity in z, conclusions, and rates throughout the affected chain.

issues.title: Missing large-σ regime in the Case 2 quadrature proof
issues.failure_explanation: With h=σ²α², the geometric term in Poissonsum2 behaves as exp(−qT), where q=4π²α/h=4π²/(σ²α). For admissible sufficiently large σ, q<1, so it is not O(e^(−T)). The desired large-σ rate instead has exponent η²T. Moreover, when β=0 and l=1, q=η² and the outer factor T cannot be absorbed into O(e^(−η²T)); a mere relabeling of the old estimate therefore does not prove the stated endpoint rate.
issues.overall_effect: The large-σ branch of the uniform quadrature theorem, especially the no-T prefactor for l=1 at β=0, is not established by the old Case 2 argument. The corresponding large-σ approximation rates inherit this gap.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Rework the final Case 2 Poisson estimate by keeping the contour contributions separate when σ>σopt. The shifted and vertical-contour terms are O(T^l e^(−T)) and hence O(e^(−η²T)) for η<1. Estimate the interpolation-pole residues directly from u(j,k)−T=α log(s_k/C)±i(2j−1)απ; for l=1 this factor is independent of T, so their sum is O(exp(−[2/(2−β)]η²T)) and therefore O(e^(−η²T)), including the endpoint β=0. Combining these estimates proves the advertised large-σ branch and allows all listed dependent rates to remain unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The old bound fails on a full admissible large-σ regime, and its coarse outer T factor cannot establish the β=0, l=1 endpoint guarantee. Recovering the exact stated rate requires a contained but nontrivial separation and refinement of the Case 2 contour and residue estimates, not a mere relabeling or constant correction. The repair stays within the existing Poisson–contour architecture and preserves the full affected chain, so it is moderate rather than serious.

issues.title: Incomplete pole inventory in the Poisson residue sum
issues.failure_explanation: In Poissonsum10 the triple sum ranges over k=0,…,m, but its residue is evaluated at u(j,0), so k does not occur in the summand. This cannot represent the contour identity eq:fourier_cpath, whose poles are u(j,k) for every k, and it omits all residues from the interpolation denominators with k≥1.
issues.overall_effect: The final Poisson estimate does not, as printed, account for all poles crossed by the contour, leaving the quadrature theorem and its dependent approximation results with a local proof gap.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In Poissonsum10, replace u(j,0) by u(j,k) in the triple residue sum, with the already stated parity-dependent Fourier sign. The existing contour identity and Lemma residual then bound every pole family and yield the same quadrature and downstream estimates.
issues.why_classification: The summation already ranges over k, eq:fourier_cpath explicitly contains the poles u(j,k), and Lemma residual estimates those same residues. Thus the absent k in the copied summand has one uniquely forced correction and requires no new inference or estimate.

issues.title: Incorrect coefficient range in the generalized LP theorem
issues.failure_explanation: The old theorem advertises N1+1 lightning coefficients indexed 0,…,N1, but eq:rat and eq:tapered2 define exactly N1 pole terms p_j for 1≤j≤N1. Its proof forms products that are again LP approximations of the form eq:rat and therefore supports the one-based family, not a coefficient attached to an undefined p_0.
issues.overall_effect: The generalized theorem's coefficient-level construction contract is inconsistent with the LP it proves, although its approximation rates are recovered by the forced one-based reading.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change both coefficient families in Theorem mainthmG from indices 0,…,N1 to 1,…,N1, consistently with the N1 poles in eq:rat and eq:tapered2. Leave the proof and all approximation rates unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The old source defines only the one-based pole family, and the theorem's product construction is explicitly said to remain an LP of that form. An additional coefficient associated with an undefined p0 is not a coherent extra guarantee, so the one-based correction is uniquely forced and purely transcriptional.

issues.title: Undefined zeroth pole in the corner-domain LP construction

failure_location.quote: the lightning poles $\{p_{k,j}\}_{j=0}^{N_1}$ are determined by the parameters

issues.failure_explanation: The old source declares the corner pole family as {p_{k,j}} for 1≤j≤N_{1,k}, consistently with eq:rat and eq:tapered2. Nevertheless, LP_cornerdomain and Theorem corner require p_{k,0}. No value or construction of p_{k,0} is supplied, so the claimed approximant is not well-defined and the counts N=N1+N2+1 and n=ℓ(N1+1)+N2 count a nonexistent pole.
issues.overall_effect: The corner theorem's promised approximant and its degree counts are ill-defined as written; the convergence rate itself is unchanged once the indexing is corrected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the source-supported one-based corner-pole convention throughout LP_cornerdomain, Theorem corner, and its proof: sum over j=1,…,N1, and correct the exact counts to N=N1+N2 and n=ℓN1+N2. Apply the same reindexing to the displayed local and global approximants; the convergence estimates then remain unchanged.
issues.why_classification: Unlike an isolated range typo in a statement, the zeroth index enters the actual approximant construction and its exact degree counts, so the construction is not executable as written. Nevertheless, the surrounding pole definitions uniquely support a short, routine systematic reindexing, with no new pole construction, proof argument, asymptotic-rate change, or meaningful loss.
